correctness.rationale: The absorption resolvent depends on allocation only via q=cd. Its survival-Laplace derivative N/D² factors as absorption-time Laplace transform times the transform of a positive three-exponential convolution because the transient generator is symmetrizable and strictly negative. This yields strict positive pointwise survival derivative for every t>0, including both allocation-boundary cases by continuity. Exact fourth-order Taylor computation and 541 independent checker assertions corroborate the formula and boundaries.

originality.rationale: The genuine addition over qualitative asymmetric-dispersal simulations and mean-persistence management criteria is strict all-horizon extinction-time stochastic dominance under fixed total directed rescue, including a sharp fourth-order onset. Full texts of the 2006 motivating article and 2014 rescue study were inspected; relevant 2001 and 2010 management sources were available as abstracts only. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Full texts of Etienne–Heesterbeek (2001) and Ross–Pollett (2010) were unavailable; any equivalent theorem inside them would take priority over this result.
Classical finite-state phase-type reliability and metapopulation stochastic-order literature may use equivalent terminology not identified in the available searches.
The exact theorem is confined to a closed two-patch CTMC and initial joint occupancy.

value.rationale: At a fixed recolonization budget a manager may care about any specific extinction deadline, not only the mean. The theorem establishes a strict full-distribution comparison with exact all-horizon optimality and an unexpectedly fourth-order short-deadline effect, while an explicit singleton-start boundary blocks overgeneralization. Natural analytical ecological benchmark; not a recommendation for real reserves without parameter validation.
